To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
liquid phase HBr treatment technology can be used as a replacement of PECVD method to form the gate insulator of MOS-mHEMT.
the HBr + UV treatment technology is highly potential for low-noise microwave power device applications.
the HBr + UV treatment method can form a high quality InAlAs gate insulator layer, which is beneficial to improve the electrical performance of MOS-mHEMT.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication and electrical characteristics of liquid-phase HBr treated MOS-mHEMT with high electrical performance.
the development of a novel liquid-phase HBr + UV illumination treatment technology to form an excellent gate insulator layer for MOS-mHEMT applications.
the liquid-phase HBr +UV treatment of the gate oxide of InAlAs / InGaAs metamorph high electron mobility transisitors (mHEMTs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the novel liquid-phase HBr + UV illumination treatment technology provides a high-quality gate dielectric layer and low surface states for the MOS-mHEMT, which is beneficial for reducing noise and enhancing the power performance.
the liquid-phase HBr +UV illumination treatment technology can be used for forming the high quality gate insulator layer of MOS-mHEMT and it can also enhance the power-added efficiency of mHEMT.
liquid-phase HBr +UV treatment technology is a promising candidate for the future development of high-performance mHEMTs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the liquid-phase HBr technology can provide a high quality gate insulator for MOS-mHEMT, and the MOS structure can be successfully fabricated.
the liquid-phase HBr technology is more suitable for the formation of a high-quality gate dielectric of the InGaAs-based device.
the liquid-phase HBr +UV illumination treatment technology can be used to form a high electrical performance gate oxide layer for InAlAs/ InGaAs MOS-mHEMT applications.

the liquid phase HBr + UV illumination treatment method can be used as a promising candidate in the future for high electrical performance MOS-mHEMT fabrication.
